question: How far do the cloud API rater and the local official procedure agree, and where do they differ (rubric/prompt vs model/infrastructure vs the procedure's own noise)?
reference: R0 = the RECORDED official verdicts of 8 sealed mute runs (the official independent blind procedure: one fresh describer per run, one fresh judge, JUDGE_RULES). This is procedure conformance, NOT human truth.

set.draw: audit/c7-pilots/calib-select.js (seeded sha256('c7-calibration'); Antidote, explains recorded, dated >= 2026-10-01, one run per book, 4 recorded PASS + 4 FAIL; P1 holdout books excluded)
set.split: DEV (2 PASS + 2 FAIL) may be used to align prompts/protocol; TEST (2 PASS + 2 FAIL) is rated ONCE at the end and changes nothing

raters.R2: cloud API, the official rubric text (scripts/lib/mute-rubric.js), one image per call
raters.R3: a re-run of the official procedure on the same images (fresh local sonnet describer per run + fresh judge) = the procedure's own noise floor
raters.R4: adjudication: on items where R2 and R0 disagree on WRONG or dead, a third independent blind chain (fresh describer + fresh judge, official rubric) decides by majority

metrics: per-item agreement on correctness, contribution, explains (% and Cohen kappa)
WRONG and dead (NONE): false positives / negatives vs R0
run-level verdict (WRONG <= 1, dead <= 5 of 30): false PASS / false FAIL vs R0
the same for R3 vs R0 = the noise floor the others are compared with

decision.policy: the cloud rater never gives a PASS alone (operator, cycle 7). It may serve as the SECOND rater only if, on TEST: its run verdict matches R0 on >= 7/8 runs AND its per-item WRONG and dead agreement with R0 is within 5 points of R3's

budget: cloud API rating via ai-budget.js (estimate); local subagent ratings are not API-billed
